text.p: - Slovenian president Milan Kucan on Monday met ambassadors of seven central European countries in order to prepare for meeting of leaders of these countries in June in Slovenia.
- Slovenia and Bolgaria will join international peacekeeping force SFOR in Bosnia this spring. With this enlargement, SFOR will include 19 countries.
- By midnight Slovenian political parties have to present their accounts on money spent on their electoral campaigns for November general election.

- Marjan Podobnik, president of the conservative Slovenian People's Party, said he will insist on the presence of all oposition parties in the next government. Prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek has to present his new government line-up by February 17 after his previous proposal failed to gain support in parliament.
- Parliament has yet to ratify 30 international agreements. Nine, which have priority should be ratified as soon as possible, parliament said.
- Slovenia's consumer price inflation in January was 1.1 percent and not 1.0 percent, the Statistics Office said after revision of figures.
- Computer hackers have caused no major damage as yet in Slovenia, a research group said. Last year there were 10 serious incidents and some 30 minor ones.
- Slovenia's ministry of science and technology signed an agreement on scientific and technological cooperation with India on Monday.

- Prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek on Monday started a new round of talks with parliamentary parties in an effort to form a new government line-up after his previous line-up failed to gain support in parliament last Thursday.
- Slovenia will build 25 km (15 miles) out of 44.5 km (27 miles) of the railway connection with neighbouring Hungary. The investment will cost Slovenia 10.4 billion tolars ($68.9 million).
